summary.headline: HUL Q1 FY27 underlying sales growth accelerated to 10% (5% volume, 5% price), with EBITDA margin at 23% within guided range.
summary.overview: HUL reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR 17,184 crores with 10% underlying sales growth, the highest in 13 quarters, split equally between volume and price. Growth accelerated from 3% in H1 FY26. EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 3,947 crores at a 23% margin, within the guided range. Reported PAT of INR 2,680 crores fell 2% YoY because of a one-off tax credit of about INR 330 crores in the base quarter; adjusted for this, PAT grew 11%. Management reaffirmed that FY27 will be better than FY26 and that the EBITDA margin will stay around the guided range, while flagging monsoon, crude and geopolitical risks.

financial_highlights.change: -2% YoY; base included ~INR 330 crore one-off tax credit
Stepped up sequentially; highest in 11 quarters

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 14% on high-single-digit UVG, the strongest in 3 years. Fabric Wash grew double digits, volume-led; Household Care (Vim Liquid) grew double digits in USG and UVG. Calibrated price increases taken on crude-linked inputs.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 12% on high-single-digit UVG. Hair Care grew double digits, volume-led; Skin Care and Colour Cosmetics grew high single digit, with Premium Skin Care at double digit and Minimalist accelerating. Health & Wellbeing (OZiva) was soft as the business transitions toward emerging demand spaces.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 4%, driven by price increases taken for palm oil inflation for a second year. Skin Cleansing grew mid single digit (Dove and Pears premium bars double digit; Bodywash double digit); soaps volumes declined mid-single digit per analyst question. Oral Care grew mid single digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 7% on mid-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew double digit volume-led; Premium Tea low-single-digit UVG. Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit (Horlicks, Boost); Boost crossed INR 1,000 crore turnover. Packaged Foods grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to be better than FY26; guidance retained, but no quarterly guidance given.
EBITDA margin expected to remain around the current guided range despite elevated commodities and currencies.
Demand environment expected to remain stable; no inflation-led demand impact seen.
Guidance is risk-adjusted for macro and portfolio risks, per management.
Capital Markets Day scheduled for September 2026 for strategy update.
capex_capacity: Haridwar and Sonepat factories recognized in WEF Global Lighthouse Network; HUL now holds 8 designations across 6 sites.
Liquids Lab of the Future in Mumbai, AI-enabled, said to cut formulation timelines by up to 6x.
Unilever Fragrance House launched in India as part of a global fragrance capability programme.
Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada with AI-enabled real-time visibility.
demand_pricing: Turnover-weighted market share gains claimed across the portfolio; management does not guide by segment.
Price increases calibrated; cost inflation roughly 10% vs pricing around 5% per analyst citation, not disputed by management.
Quick commerce grew 40-50% per management, with new pack architecture; GT growth stepped up led by small towns and rural.
Rural and urban both growing robustly; mass and premium both competitive, with premiumization in line with market trend.
Tea early-season read shows inflationary trend; pricing decisions to follow buying season.

qa_highlights.question: Has the outlook tone changed versus last quarter given monsoon and geopolitical concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change; it remains well positioned, and is only cautioning on how the volatile economic scenario pans out.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mid-single-digit soaps volume decline, and what is market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to palm oil inflation over two years; it is focusing on premiumization (Dove, Pears double digit, Bodywash double digit) and does not disclose segment share, saying it is winning turnover-weighted share overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is A&P under-investment happening to protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is at its highest in 11-12 quarters, with better ROI from AI-enabled programmes and media procurement savings, so like-for-like comparisons are not strictly valid.

qa_highlights.question: Is the El Nino and monsoon risk material to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a difficult versus good agriculture year moves GDP by 50-60 bps; MSP hikes of 5-6% insulate rural income, and a rainfall deficit of about 15% is seen as not meaningfully impacting the economy.

qa_highlights.question: At what crude level can 23% margin be held without further price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a precise crude threshold, but said it can maintain margins with about half of inflation passed through and that crude of $75-100/bbl is manageable; $140-160 would be a different discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quick commerce slowdown affecting HUL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QCom grew 40-50% and the channel remains structurally attractive, with new entrants and tailored assortments and pack architecture.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (palm oil, crude-linked derivatives, tea) and the pace of calibrated pricing needed to hold 23% EBITDA margin.
Soaps volume decline under palm oil-led price pressure and value competition in soaps and liquids.
Monsoon progression (rainfall deficit cited at about 15%) and El Nino impact on rural demand.
OZiva growth moderation in Health & Wellbeing and the stated transition of the business.
Management's shift from prior quarter's language on navigating volatility to cautioning on monsoon and geopolitics; watch wording at the September Capital Markets Day.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and execution, with explicit caution on macro, crude and monsoon. Management was reluctant to give quarterly or segment-level guidance and deflected questions on soap market share and crude thresholds.
key_quotes: Our growth trajectory has strengthened from 3% in the first half of FY'26 to 10% in this quarter.
we remain confident that FY '27 will be better than FY'26.
We, therefore, expect EBITDA Margin to remain around the current guided range.
the barriers to entry may have got reduced, Priya, what you keep saying, but the barrier to scale has only gone up

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 will be better than FY26 and EBITDA margin around the ~23% guided range, but gave no quantified FY27 revenue growth and no specific capacity, orders or contracts behind it; growth came from Q1 USG of 10% (5% volume, 5% price) plus claimed share gains and quick commerce growth of 40-50%.
